correctness.rationale: For every m>=3, root polytope R_m=Delta_(m-1)-Delta_(m-1)={x:sum x_i=0, sum |x_i|<=2}. For u in H_m with positive mass T and a_i=(-u_i)^+, b_j=(u_j)^+, the exact one-sided derivative at root e_i-e_j gives illumination iff a_i+b_j>T; derivative zero stays on boundary locally and cannot enter later by convexity. Two illuminated edges with distinct source and target contradict total masses, so every illuminated vertex set is a directed star of size <=m-1. Equality forces one sign on the unique star center and all other coordinates of opposite strict sign, giving the full outgoing/incoming stars. Vertex counting yields both I and finite-direction I* >=m; m outgoing stars illuminate all vertices and hence every boundary point by active supporting-facet inclusion. At fractional optimum all positively weighted directions are full stars and each vertex receives exactly one unit, so alpha_i+beta_j=1 for i!=j, forcing alpha_i=theta, beta_j=1-theta. Ordinary m-unit covers require theta in {0,1}. Independent exact integer-grid probes m=3..5 corroborate the star bound; proof is analytic for all m.
